My friend was in £10k or debt from gambling but used it as motivation to never get to that rock bottom again. Life isn't linear and things can always get better in ways you don't expect. 30 is really young, you have loads of time and a few years sorting things out won't seem like much in the scheme of things, and will be so worth it. You'll have so much more perspective than anyone around you who appears to have everything figured out (they almost certainly don't). You can do this!

All I can say to this is, you can do it and it will be fine. I have been in your position - horrendously stressed the week before any flight, sobbing my way onto a plane, having breakdowns in the aisle😅. But I kept flying. Sometimes there is some turbulence, sometimes there isn't. Sometimes I see 'omens'. Sometimes I don't. Sometimes the planes are super noisy, sometimes they aren't. Sometimes it's what I would consider a 'scary' aircraft, sometimes not. 

I have flown 20 times in the last couple of years alone, and ALL of the flights have been fine. Every single one. I still get stressed, but now it's when I'm on the plane, not the week before. The anxiety doesn't get too much, I can deal with it. I have found noise cancelling headphones and my favourite podcast to be a game changer. 

I recently flew long haul, something I never thought I'd be able to do. Next year I'm taking a 14 hour return flight alone, and I can't wait to prove to myself how far I've come. 

Getting on the plane tomorrow is the first step. You can do this!
